Subject: Prompt-set A/B gating — exception request and coordination

Team —

We ran the pre-canary evals for the new prompt-set A (short-context medical summarization) and are seeing a quality regression vs baseline on a small but important slice: complex multi-recommendation notes (severity: medium). The automated signal flagged a 6.2% drop on our primary metric and several manual checks surfaced hallucination patterns on medication lists.

Given StellarHealth's scheduled onboarding next week (DL-2027-0041) and DocuCare's procurement timeline, I want to propose a temporary gating exception: hold the full A/B rollout to 10% and expand the test coverage (add 300 more prompts focusing on polypharmacy cases) while we triage.

Attachments: eval_quickcheck.csv (summary)

Requesting:
- Engineering: quick root-cause & proposed hotfix or config rollback threshold.
- Product (Tessa): updated acceptance criteria and rollback thresholds for this prompt-set.
- GTM (Rishi): customer-facing messaging if we delay the scheduled canary.

Can we sync on next steps and owners in the next 2 hours?

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Prompt-set A/B gating — exception request and coordination

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the flag. Quick summary from infra/engine: the regression correlates with the long-tail prompts that include nested bullet lists and medication shorthand (e.g., "ASA 81mg qd"). Two hypotheses: the new decoding tuning + cache warming strategy for A is increasing token-level over-generation on constrained contexts; and a subtle tokenization mismatch with the latest tokenizer merge for medical abbreviations.

What I did so far:
- Ran a focused inference sweep on 800 seed prompts (attached eval_quickcheck.csv shows per-prompt deltas).
- Re-ran with previous decoding params (pre-A tuning) — performance returns to baseline on ~93% of cases.
- Started a quick tokenization fix branch that normalizes common med shorthands at input preprocessing.

Immediate ask: allow us to keep rollout at 10% or pause expansion while we A) validate the preprocessing patch and B) run the extended 300-case test set. If the patch restores metrics to within the acceptance delta (<=2% relative delta) we can resume. Otherwise we should rollback to the prior decoding config.

I can have a validation matrix and PR for the preprocessing patch by EOD.

— Dev
Senior SW Eng, Serving Runtime
